newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU farm chief leaves for N.Zealand, Australia talks.
newsitem.headline: EU farm chief leaves for N.Zealand, Australia talks.

text.p: EU Farm Commissioner Franz Franz Fischler flew on Friday to New Zealand and Australia for wide-ranging farm trade talks until February 9, Commission officials said.
In both countries Fischler is expected to defend EU farm policy against calls for bigger cuts in subsidies and faster opening of its protected market.
In New Zealand, Fischler will meet Prime Minister James Bolger, Agriculture Minister Lockwood Smith and foreign Minister Don McKinnon.

Topics will include future EU farm reform, impact of EU expansion eastwards on agriculture, multilateral farm trade issues and the next round of farm trade negotiations under the World Trade Organisation starting in 1999 and bilateral trade.
In Australia, Fischler will discuss the same issues with Primary Industries Minister John Anderson and Trade Minister Tim Fischer.
Anderson will in addition review progress in negotiations on veterinary inspection standards agreement, wheat gluten, EU wheat and other export subsidies, as well as WTO issues.
Fischler will raise problems over EU pigmeat and cheese exports and countervailing duties on EU farm products.
